key_insight: High-resolution multiphase LBM simulations show that wall-impact pressures in dam-break waves are strongly controlled by wave-front deflection, small corner vortices, and local air entrainment.
engineering_relevance: Accurately modeling air entrainment and near-wall shear is essential for predicting impact loads on vertical structures and avoiding misleading estimates of extreme pressures.
method: Two-phase lattice Boltzmann method for air–water flow
Direct numerical simulation of dam-break wave impact on vertical walls with resolved solid–fluid interfaces
evidence_signal: The study compares high-resolution simulations under no-slip and free-slip wall treatments and links pressure peaks and cavity formation to local flow features seen in the simulations.
watch_item: Large trapped air cavities may depend on wall-boundary modeling assumptions, so conclusions about jet breakup and entrainment should be checked against the chosen no-slip/free-slip implementation.
paper_title: Vortex dynamics and air entrainment in dam break wave impacting on vertical walls: A multiphase lattice Boltzmann study
